title: Lorenzo's clarinets: ebony, keys and his family of clarinets
summary: Tio describes his brother's ebony clarinet with open keys and trill keys, his A, B-flat, C, E-flat and D clarinets, and a bassoon played at Tranchina's.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Now there were a few things that probably Ralph would like to ask too, Ralph's trying to learn clarinet a little, about your brother, do you remember what kind of an instrument he had? Anything about his instrument, if it was how many keys, or if it was Albert or system, or what kind of a clarinet it was? What maker or anything at all?
No, it was an Ebony, black Ebony, but I didn't know the name, but I forgot about it.
Would it be something like a French name, something like Buffet or something like that?
There's one of them, yes, but there's another one besides that Buffet, there was a... Oh, I can't see right now.
There's a French Selmer, there's a lot of French makes that we don't even know about, I guess.
Well, the instrument in them days, like, they didn't have as many keys, that is, metal keys, as the instrument of today. A hundred percent of that was open keys, you know, few metal keys.
I wondered if, if you could remember if it had those ring keys, or holes, on both the top and...
No, on the bottom, but not the top.
Uh-huh. They had the ring, they had the holes in the top.
And you had the rings on the bottom. With the trill keys.
The trill keys, did it have two or three?

Two. Two trill keys. Mostly it would just be two. That is the old instrument, and then they came with the three. And they had three trillings on the above, on the above part of the clarinet. They had also two, but then they later on got a three.

So I don't know. I wondered if you, if you knew, of course he would be playing, as you say, B flat all the time, but I wondered if you, if he ever played the E flat in the parades. Oh yeah. Yeah. He noticed that picture. I remember that, he got an E flat on that picture.

On that picture, yeah. Oh, I hope to tell you. On the little band, I mean, on the, I don't know, that's fine. Yeah, right here. I could just, I never knew. Did he play it? E flat, isn't he? Oh, up here, sure. Oh yeah, sure. We can see. I saw that, as soon as you all opened it. Yeah, I never noticed that. I've seen that big. E flat. Now he had a whole family of clarinet.
He had a B clarinet, he had a B flat clarinet, A and a C. And you know, E flat, and he had a D. Oh, a D.
D clarinet. D, I don't believe I ever saw a D.

It's a heavy toned instrument, like the A clarinet. Yes. And the C clarinet is probably supposed to be mostly a youngster that is trying. A very toned, very soft toned instrument, the C clarinet. Then you got the E flat clarinet with a high, very high pitch. Did you know that? Yes. The E flat has a very high pitch. Now the D clarinet, they have a very deep tone and it has also a little bell on the part of it. Like an outdoor. Like an outdoor. Yeah, that's a D clarinet. Yeah. Well he had one also. Yeah. My brother had a D clarinet. He had a little bar. He used to play bassoon, but mostly when he was playing at Felice Crencini, Felice Crencini found him with the bassoon. Yeah. Yeah. He had a pretty expensive piece of instrument. Yeah, that was a big, yeah. Unless you couldn't very well buy it, but you wanted. Well, Felice Crencini used to love to hear him play that and he used to, he fought it to you. You know who Felice Crencini was. Yeah, that's it. The nightclub down at the lake. Yeah. He managed to play.
